decisions.reason: Simultaneous charging and integrated-board power-path scope do not change the battery connector's physical placement or accessibility constraints.
The source establishes charging and rail needs for the integrated-board context but does not revise or remove the existing modular interboard interfaces.
The source concerns normal battery-and-USB power-path behavior and does not change the separate standalone main-board USB supply used without the power board.
The electrical requirement for simultaneous charging and 3.3V/5V rails does not alter the modular power board's mechanical layout constraints.
The source does not change the panel button connector, its location, or its PWRON control behavior.
Requiring 3.3V and 5V rails does not modify the existing requirement to monitor those rails or its INA3221 measurement topology.
Inviting a simpler power-path suggestion does not establish a new sourcing policy or change the existing integrated-board cost and JLCPCB Basic-component policy.
The source reiterates the need for a 3.3V rail but does not change the existing 3.4V DCDC1 configuration or its Schottky-drop compensation requirement.
The source requires availability of a 5V rail but does not alter its GPIO switching, boost converter, powered loads, or shutdown behavior.
The charging and rail requirements do not change the AXP2101 exposed-pad thermal-transfer requirement.
Simultaneous charging and operation do not resolve or modify the battery connector's series, pinout, mounting type, or existing pinout ambiguity.
The power-path decision does not change the selected ESP32 module or its full through-hole breakout requirements.
